thread:
maria: heads up — multiple customers in APAC reporting 503s + big latency spikes since 02:12 UTC. pattern looks like requests are being routed to us-west fallback a lot.
jon_sre: seeing same on infra side. load balancer logs show a sudden increase in cross-region fallbacks at ~02:10. healthcheck for ap-east pool was flapping.
kevin_platform: can you paste the lb routing decision logs? curious if this is sticky-fallback behavior or full failover.
maria: here's an anonymized snippet from routing-decisions.log:
```
[02:09:58] req_id=abc123 src=apac region=ap-east prefer=ap-east route -> ap-east
[02:10:01] req_id=abc124 src=apac region=ap-east prefer=ap-east route -> us-west (fallback, sticky=true)
[02:10:05] req_id=abc125 src=apac region=ap-east prefer=ap-east route -> us-west
```
ana_support: customers report auth failures after retrying — tokens appear to be region-scoped. when requests hit us-west they fail 401 and clients retry, seeing billing double-charges for token refresh attempts.
lee_cs: customer reported: "we got 503s then some requests succeeded from us-west but our client logged invalid_token and we were billed for two calls" — they provided curl command.
maria: repro curl (redacted):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Region: ap-east" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
jon_sre: timeline: ap-east health checks started flapping at 02:09 -> autoscaler removed a node group at 02:11 -> lb started fallback policy at 02:10 -> sticky fallback set to 600s caused new connections to continue hitting us-west even after some nodes returned at 02:16.
kevin_platform: sticky fallback TTL is 600s by default for that policy — that explains sustained cross-region routing. smaller TTL would have reduced primary re-attach time.
maria: impact: ~7 customers affected, higher latency (200-800ms extra), ~3 reported auth errors and billing anomalies, support tickets elevated to P2.
ana_support: quick mitigation: disable sticky fallback for ap-east pool and force immediate re-evaluation. can ops do a config toggle?
ops-bot: runbook trigger: region-failover -> notify on-call -> checkpoint created.
jon_sre: toggled sticky_fallback=false at 02:24 UTC. flushing lb session cache for ap-east. monitoring.
kevin_platform: also rolled a config to reduce fallback-ttl to 30s for now.
maria: after toggle, routing revert started ~02:26 and most traffic back in ap-east by 02:30. latency normalized. auth failures reduced once traffic returned to primary region.
lee_cs: told customers the temporary workaround and created crediting plan for customers who saw billing duplicates. CS to track reimbursements.
ana_support: collecting repro steps from affected customers for postmortem. we need exact request ids and timestamps to audit billing.
jon_sre: root cause (prelim): brief control-plane overload during a rolling deploy of an autoscaler agent caused node health probe flapping. fallbacks triggered; sticky-fallback TTL combined with region-scoped tokens caused 401s on fallback->primary transitions.
kevin_platform: long-term fixes suggested:
- make tokens region-agnostic (or accept cross-region validation) for short window
- make fallback sticky TTL adaptive based on probe confidence
- improve autoscaler rollout health guard (pause fallbacks during control-plane instability)
- add billing dedupe for retried token-exchange calls
maria: action items assigned:
- jon_sre: postmortem + timeline + logs (due EOD)
- kevin_platform: routing policy change proposal + config defaults (RFC by EOW)
- ana_support/lee_cs: compile customer list, credits, comms draft (ASAP)
- infra: gating autoscaler deploys behind extra health checks
ops-bot: postmortem checklist created: incident number INC-2026-452
maria: customer communications: initial message sent at 03:05 UTC explaining cause + mitigation + credits promise. will follow with detailed postmortem later.
jon_sre: note for postmortem: attach samples of routing-decisions.log, lb session cache dump, token validation traces, and billing request ids.
kevin_platform: I'll draft the RFC for adaptive fallback TTL. any objections to lowering default sticky TTL to 60s while we evaluate? :thinking:
maria: no objections. do it in a canary first.
ana_support: logging: please add an explicit flag in response headers when a request is served from fallback region: `X-Served-Region: us-west (fallback)` so support can quickly triage next time.
kevin_platform: agree, I'll add header in next deploy.
lee_cs: thanks everyone. CS has the customer list and will send followups this morning.
maria: closing notes: incident contained; SLO impact <1h for most customers. followups scheduled. thanks to the on-call and support teams for quick mitigation. :heart:
deploy-bot: deploy logged: cfg/routing/disable-sticky-fallback v1.3 by jon_sre @02:24 UTC
ops-bot: incident closed to active monitoring at 03:45 UTC.
